title: Memory in Deep Time-Series Models
abstract: arXiv:2609.06006v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Deep learning for time series has progressed through successive architectural paradigms, from recurrent networks and transformers to structured state-space models, retrieval-augmented predictors, foundation models, and tool-using agents. These developments are typically studied in isolation, organized by architecture or modeling era. We argue that they can instead be viewed through a common question of \emph{how does a time-series model retain and access information beyond its immediate input?} This question is motivated by a fundamental limitation of conventional time-series modeling: information relevant to a prediction may lie far beyond a feasible input window, while compressing history into a fixed-size state can discard information that may become useful later. translated_title: 深度时间序列模型中的记忆
translated_abstract: 时间序列深度学习经历了多个架构范式的相继演进，从循环网络和Transformer，到结构化状态空间模型、检索增强预测器、基础模型以及使用工具的智能体。这些发展通常被孤立地研究，按架构或建模时代来组织。我们认为，可以通过一个共同的问题来审视它们：时间序列模型如何在直接输入之外保留和访问信息？这个问题的动机来自传统时间序列建模的一个根本局限：与预测相关的信息可能位于可行输入窗口之外很远的地方，而将历史压缩为固定大小的状态可能会丢弃之后可能变得有用的信息。我们将这一挑战表述为一个“记忆”问题，并将现有的时间序列方法沿着一个从内部记忆（编码在参数和固定大小的状态中）到外部记忆的谱系进行组织……
tldr: 本文提出用一个统一的“记忆”视角来重新审视时间序列深度学习中从循环网络到基础模型等各类架构范式，将其视为对“模型如何在直接输入之外保留和访问信息”这一共同问题的不同解决方案。
en_tdlr: This paper reframes diverse time-series deep learning paradigms—from recurrent networks to foundation models—through a unified memory perspective, viewing them as different solutions to the common question of how a model retains and accesses information beyond its immediate input.
